title: Testing the Problem of Time with Cold Atoms: Entropic Time Emergence in a Mini-Universe
source: Barontini, G. Physical Review Research 8, L022047 (2026); arXiv:2509.07745
key_claim: A hermetically sealed Bose-Einstein condensate of ~24,000 ultracold 87Rb atoms can self-order its dynamics using an internally constructed 'entropic time' derived from coarse-grained entropy flow between observed ('bright') and unobserved ('dark') sectors, without reference to external laboratory clocks, and follows an effective Schrodinger equation parameterized by this internal time.
empirical_status: Controlled laboratory experiment with repeated Big Bang/Big Crunch cycles; quantitative reproduction of mean-field evolution using entropic time; negligible dissipation on experimental timescale (~100 ms)
methodology: Magneto-optical trap; crossed optical dipole trap (1070 nm + 1550 nm, ~2π×(25,70,70) Hz); digital micromirror device barrier (675 nm, ~8 μm width); effective non-Hermitian Gross-Pitaevskii Hamiltonian; entropic time definition τ(λ) = (σ/k_B) ∫_λ |dS/dφ| |dφ|
cross_layer_patterns: Internal Entropy as Clock (subsystem coarse-graining drives temporal ordering)
Structured Suppression of Dominant Mode (external laboratory clock eliminated)
Big Bang / Big Crunch Cyclicity (bright sector expansion and recollapse)
snn_analog: Bright/dark sector partitioning mirrors neuromorphic reservoir/dark-sector architectures; entropy flow between subsystems acts as an internal clock analogous to free-energy minimization time in active inference systems
integration_notes: Provides first controlled experimental testbed for relational-time constructions in the Wheeler-DeWitt framework. The entropic time definition is formally similar to semiclassical WKB time but uses thermodynamic entropy rather than a Hamilton-Jacobi function. Directly extensible to more complex systems including black-hole analogues and false-vacuum decay experiments.
references: Barontini, G. (2026). Testing the problem of time with cold atoms. Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047.
Wheeler, B. S. & DeWitt, B. S. (1967). Battle of the giants: the quantum theory of gravity. Phys. Rev. 160, 1113.
